tools.name: Invidious
tools.blurb: Opens YouTube through a public instance with no ads, no tracking and no JavaScript required, though the project says plainly that it does not use YouTube's official APIs and takes no responsibility for the third-party instances it lists.

tools.name: G'MIC 4.0
tools.blurb: Brings the filter count to 644 with six new ones in this release, among them Pixel Stretch and Heightfield Warp, but it is a plugin rather than an app: you run it inside GIMP, Krita, Photoshop or Affinity Photo, from the command line, or in a browser at G'MIC Online.

tools.name: Elevators, an interactive explainer
tools.blurb: Lets you set building height, car count and passenger flow, then watch LOOK, destination dispatch and other algorithms rearrange the wait-time histogram, which is the whole of it: this is a browser essay with simulators inside, not an app you keep.

tools.name: Yamanote 3D
tools.blurb: Puts you inside an E235 carriage on Tokyo's Yamanote loop, where you walk the car, sit down, listen to the station announcements and step off at a stop, with nothing to win or finish: its maker pitches it as calm background for studying or working.

tools.name: EssayKraft
tools.blurb: A paginated writing app with automatic citations, built-in reference lookup and DOCX export, bought once with no subscription and no account, though the App Store listing asks for macOS 26 or iPadOS 26, which rules out older machines.

tools.name: Gander
tools.blurb: Opens PDFs, Word and Excel files, images, video, audio, Markdown and code entirely offline without asking for storage permission, though you sideload the APK from GitHub because it is not on the Play Store or F-Droid.

tools.name: mectrics
tools.blurb: Folds CPU, memory, battery, network, disk, GPU and fan readings into a single menu bar item that stays quiet until a threshold holds, and its own launch notes concede it goes less deep than paid rivals such as iStat Menus.

tools.name: Focus Room
tools.blurb: Put focusroom.club/ in front of any YouTube URL and the video reopens as a distraction-free course with transcript search and timestamped notes, though launch-day testers hit YouTube quota errors and the notes cannot be exported yet.

tools.name: Kaneo
tools.blurb: Runs kanban boards and issue tracking on a machine you own from a Docker Compose file, and its makers state the trade-off plainly: a deliberately minimal design with fewer features than Jira or Linear.

tools.name: SoundGate Guitar
tools.blurb: It listens through the microphone and draws what you are playing on a live fretboard, with an AI tutor that answers questions and builds practice routines, plus a tuner and metronome; it is an Apple-only app, so Android players are out of luck.

tools.name: Yap, on-device dictation for macOS
tools.blurb: Press a shortcut, talk, press it again, and your words appear in whatever text field you were in, using Apple's built-in speech APIs with no model to download and no network calls; it needs macOS 26 or later on Apple Silicon, and Intel Macs are deliberately not supported.

tools.name: CheapFoodMap
tools.blurb: A map of meals under $10 across a dozen featured cities including New York, Chicago, Houston and Los Angeles, with a price-verified date shown on each spot; the entries are crowdsourced, so coverage thins out fast once you pan away from the big cities.

tools.name: tale.fyi
tools.blurb: One link opens a whole book, keeps your place on the device, and lets you swap between reading and listening; an account is optional and only syncs progress, but the library is public domain material from Project Gutenberg, Standard Ebooks and LibriVox, so nothing modern is on the shelf.

tools.name: TokenTown
tools.blurb: Type a prompt and watch a single token travel through an isometric city where each district is one stage of a language model, from tokenizing to attention to sampling; the model is deliberately tiny and its weights are random and untrained, so the words it produces are noise and only the machinery is real.

workflows.title: Back up one folder to every cloud account you own, with a single command
workflows.dek: One union remote Faisal Rasool's Saturday walkthrough installs rclone, authenticates each account with rclone config, then merges Google Drive, Dropbox and the rest into one union remote so a single copy command fans a folder out to all of them.
needs: rclone, free on Windows, Mac, Linux

workflows.title: Follow 38 hand-checked blogs at once by importing a single OPML file
workflows.dek: One file, 38 feeds The directory behind a 140-point post on today's Hacker News front page hands out its whole membership as OPML for any reader to import in one step, and joining it costs a badge on your homepage and a submitted URL, checked for the link back.
needs: A site of your own, only to join

workflows.title: Set three free apps running this weekend and then leave them alone
workflows.dek: Watch, sync, encrypt Dibakar Ghosh's weekend list pairs Changedetection.io for price and stock alerts (free self-hosted in Docker, or $9 a month hosted) with Syncthing for device-to-device syncing that skips the cloud, and Cryptomator for encrypting files before they ever reach it.

workflows.title: Record an episode this week and hear it published on a feed running since 2005
workflows.dek: Book the slot first Hacker Public Radio lets a contributor reserve a calendar date up to a year out, then emails a one-time upload link that expires in 15 minutes, and it takes phone recordings as readily as FLAC.
needs: A topic you can talk through
A free slot on the calendar

workflows.title: Start Microsoft's free AI curriculum, 24 lessons at your own pace
workflows.dek: Begin at lesson zero The lessons run from symbolic AI through neural networks, computer vision and language in Jupyter notebooks, and the README is blunt that business applications, classic machine learning and chatbots are out of scope.
needs: A GitHub account to fork it

workflows.title: Run a 26B AI model offline on a small Mac laptop
workflows.dek: Big model, small Mac TurboFieldfare keeps only the essential weights in memory and streams the rest from storage, so Gemma 4 26B answers inside about 2 GB of RAM, at 5.1 to 6.3 tokens per second on an 8 GB M2 MacBook Air and 31 to 35 on an M5.
needs: Text only: no images or tools

workflows.title: Make a landlord's dumb air conditioner smart for about $15
workflows.dek: Renter-safe automation A stepper motor clamped to the existing dial, driven by an ESP32 talking to Home Assistant over MQTT, switches an analog window unit on and off without modifying the unit or risking the security deposit.
needs: ESP32 and a stepper motor, about $15
Home Assistant and an MQTT broker

workflows.title: Put a jailbroken Kindle on your home network with Tailscale
workflows.dek: Kindle, meet your server The updated Tailscale KUAL app adds proxy and kernel TUN modes, and a KOReader plugin, so the reader can pull books straight from a machine at home, though Tailscale calls it community code on a very unofficial device state and warns 11th-generation Kindles have plugin trouble.
needs: A Tailscale account and auth key
